capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.descrip: In Restricted Mode, Connect Codex and Connect Gemini CLI do not write the project config: checking that git will not commit the token means running git in the workspace, which runs the repository's own hooks. The `codex mcp add` / `gemini mcp add` command is offered instead. The chat is unavailable: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Pi load the project's own configuration, which can run commands.
configuration.focusLockIndicator.enabled: Enable/disable the floating indicator that shows when focused in the AI browser.
configuration.useIntegratedBrowser.descr: Open URLs in VS Code's built-in browser rather than the HoverDeck webview panel. The built-in browser is what the element-picker commands attach to, and it supports clipboard shortcuts, find in page and DevTools that the panel cannot. Turn it off only if you specifically want the panel.
configuration.searchEngine.description: Search engine used when the address bar input is a search term rather than a URL. Set to 'none' to disable address bar search.

configuration.mcp.enabled.description: Run a local MCP server so Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and VS Code chat can drive the integrated browser. It listens on loopback only and requires a per-workspace token.
configuration.mcp.disabledFeatures.descr: Parts of the MCP server agents may not use: their tools are left out of the tool list and refuse a call. `sounds` (chat_play_sound), `alerts` (chat_alert), `cards` (chat_notify, chat_progress, chat_update_plan, chat_present_result, chat_present_json, chat_cite), `keepAwake`, `chatControl` (pause, resume, stop an agent), `recording` (browser_recording_*), `annotations` (browser_annotations_*), `cookies`, `editor` (editor_*). Read from your user settings only. Also in Chat Settings → MCP.
configuration.mcp.port.description: First port to try for the MCP server. Left unset, each window derives its own first choice from the workspace path, within the 20 ports starting here, so a window keeps the same port across restarts and a saved config does not go stale. Set it explicitly and the window starts exactly here instead. Either way it walks on until it finds a free one.

configuration.updateCheck.enabled.descri: Look for new releases of HoverDeck in the [repository](https://github.com/Denis-Davidoff/hoverdeck) and show a notification when one is out. This extension is installed from a VSIX, so nothing else updates it. Once it has reached GitHub it waits six hours before asking again; it announces each release once, and says nothing when there is no update.

configuration.logins.enabled.description: Save logins and passkeys for pages in the integrated browser, in VS Code's secret storage (encrypted by the operating system: Keychain, DPAPI or the Secret Service). On Linux with no keyring available, VS Code keeps secrets in memory only, per window, so they are gone when the window closes. Turned off, nothing is injected into pages, nothing is offered or filled, and passkeys are off — saved logins can still be managed, exported and imported.
configuration.logins.offerToSave.descrip: After a sign-in that went through, offer to save the login, or to update a saved password that changed. The offer is a status bar item; nothing covers the page.
configuration.logins.showSuggestions.des: Show a status bar item while the page in front of you has a sign-in form and a login is saved for it. `Cmd+Shift+L` / `Ctrl+Shift+L` fills either way.
Fill a sign-in form as soon as it appears, when exactly one login is saved for that exact address and the fields are empty. Off by default: a page then receives your password without you asking.
configuration.passkeys.enabled.descripti: Sign in with passkeys stored in HoverDeck, and save new ones a site creates. Every passkey ceremony in the page asks you first, and the tab's own authenticators (a security key, a phone) are reached by choosing "Use a security key or another device" in that prompt. A frame from another site, such as an embedded payment confirmation or sign-in widget, is not reached: its ceremony gets no prompt and fails after its own timeout while this is on. Turning this off hands those back to the browser.

configuration.chat.remoteTerminalShell.d: Let the HoverDeck Chrome side panel and the HoverDeck Server website open a **plain shell** terminal tab on this machine. Needs `#hoverdeck.chat.remoteTerminal#` as well. Off by default: a shell runs any command as you.
configuration.chat.remoteTerminalAgent.d: Let the HoverDeck Chrome side panel and the HoverDeck Server website open an **agent's own CLI** (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Pi) in a terminal tab on this machine. Needs `#hoverdeck.chat.remoteTerminal#` as well. Off by default.
configuration.chat.remoteTerminal.descri: Let the HoverDeck Chrome side panel and the HoverDeck Server website open, watch and, once they take control, type into terminal tabs on this machine. The website works only on connections with a workspace password (end-to-end encrypted); each connection asks once, and only terminals marked "Allow remote access" (or opened from Chrome or the website) are shared. The website is a watcher by default and takes control with a lease; your own typing in VS Code always takes it back. Encryption does not protect against a server operator who changes the website itself.
configuration.chat.terminalLimit.descrip: How many terminal tabs the HoverDeck chat keeps open at once, from 1 to 20. A terminal tab is a real shell on this machine, in the folder of the conversation in front; closing the tab ends it.
configuration.chat.tabLimit.description: How many conversations the HoverDeck chat keeps open as tabs at once, from 1 to 30. Each Claude Code tab runs a `claude` process of its own, and tabs working at once spend your plan's limits at once. Lowering it closes nothing; `+` comes back once enough tabs are closed.
configuration.chat.claudePath.descriptio: Path to the `claude` executable the chat uses. Empty finds it on `PATH`, in the usual install locations, or inside the Claude Code extension. Machine-wide only: a workspace cannot set it, since it names a program to run.
configuration.chat.viewMode.description: How much of the agents' work the HoverDeck chat shows — also the View Mode row of the chat's approval menu. **Minimal** shows only your messages and the replies: each message's tool calls, thinking and answered approvals fold under one line that counts them and says what the agent is doing now; click that line to open them for that message. **Compact** shows every tool call, folded. **Standard** shows every tool call unfolded, with its input and output.
configuration.chat.viewMode.minimal: Only messages and replies; each message's work folded under one summary line.
configuration.chat.viewMode.standard: Every tool call shown unfolded, with its input and output.
configuration.chat.collapseToolCalls.dep: Replaced by `#hoverdeck.chat.viewMode#`. Still read while View Mode is not set: off reads as Standard, on as Compact.
configuration.chat.collapseToolCalls.des: Deprecated: replaced by the View Mode setting (Minimal, Compact, Standard), also in the chat's approval menu. Read only while View Mode is not set — on reads as Compact (tool calls folded), off as Standard (unfolded).
configuration.chat.voiceLanguage.descrip: The language voice messages are transcribed in, as a BCP 47 tag such as `ru-RU` or `en-US`. Empty: the first of the Mac's preferred languages that macOS can transcribe on the device. Voice messages need macOS 26 or later.
configuration.chat.opencodePath.descript: Path to the `opencode` executable the chat uses. Empty finds it on `PATH`, in `~/.opencode/bin` (the installer's folder), npm's and nvm's usual locations, or in Homebrew. Machine-wide only: a workspace cannot set it, since it names a program to run.
configuration.chat.piPath.description: Path to the `pi` executable the chat uses. Empty finds it on `PATH`, in `~/.local/bin`, `~/.pi/agent/bin`, npm's and nvm's usual locations, or in Homebrew. Pi's launcher needs `node` on `PATH` or beside it. Machine-wide only: a workspace cannot set it, since it names a program to run.
configuration.chat.geminiPath.descriptio: Path to the `gemini` executable the chat uses. Empty finds it on `PATH`, in npm's and nvm's usual locations, or in Homebrew. Machine-wide only: a workspace cannot set it, since it names a program to run.
configuration.chat.openrouterEndpoint.de: The OpenRouter API address the chat sends requests, and your API key, to. Empty uses `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`. Only `https` addresses, or `http` on this computer (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`), are accepted; anything else makes OpenRouter unavailable. Machine-wide only: a workspace cannot set it, since the key goes to this address.
configuration.chat.codexPath.description: Path to the `codex` executable the chat uses. Empty finds it on `PATH`, in the usual install locations, or inside the Codex extension. Machine-wide only: a workspace cannot set it, since it names a program to run.

configuration.chat.sound.enabled.descrip: Play a sound in the HoverDeck chat when an agent finishes its work. This is the default; the speaker button beside the usage meter switches it for the chat view.
configuration.chat.sound.activeChat.desc: Play the finish sound even when the conversation is selected and visible in the active window. Off by default; background chats and inactive windows still play a sound when sound is enabled.
configuration.chat.sound.name.descriptio: Which sound plays when an agent finishes.
configuration.chat.sound.repeat.descript: How many times the finish sound plays in a row, 1 to 5.
configuration.chat.sound.volume.descript: Volume of that sound, 0 to 200; above 100 is louder than full volume used to be.
configuration.chat.notifications.enabled: Show a system notification (macOS Notification Center, Windows, Linux `notify-send`) when an agent in the HoverDeck chat finishes. Chrome and the website show the browser's own.
configuration.chat.sound.githubRun.descr: Which sound plays when a GitHub Actions run you rang the bell for (in the chat's GitHub tab) ends; `none` for silence. Uses the volume of `hoverdeck.chat.sound.volume`.
configuration.chat.notifications.githubR: Show a system notification when a GitHub Actions run you rang the bell for ends, whether or not the window is focused.
configuration.chat.notifications.onlyWhe: Only notify while the VS Code window (or the Chrome or website page) is not focused.
config.chat.visibleTurns.description: How many of your messages, with the agents' replies to them, a chat shows at first in VS Code, the Chrome side panel and on the website. Earlier ones load when you scroll to the top or press "Show earlier messages" (this many more each time), and are dropped again after a minute at the end of the chat. Fewer means less memory and a faster remote connection.

configuration.security.confirmNewSites.d: Before an agent opens a site it has not been to in this conversation (`browser_navigate`), ask — showing the whole address, since a page or a file the agent read can tell it to open an address that carries what it read. Localhost and the site the tab is already on are not asked about. Turning this off lets agents open any http or https address without a question.
configuration.security.hideOtherChromeTa: When HoverDeck is connected to your own Google Chrome profile, agents do not see or act on the tabs you opened yourself (your mail, your bank) — only tabs opened through HoverDeck, tabs those opened, and a tab you share. Turning this off shows agents every tab of that Chrome.
configuration.security.protectSecretFiel: Agents may not type or fill into password, one-time-code or payment card fields (`browser_fill`, `browser_type`); you type those yourself. Turning this off lets an agent enter them — and any page it is on, including one that asked for them.
configuration.security.markPageContent.d: Put a note before page text, markup, snapshots and console output an agent reads, saying it is data from a web page and not instructions. Turning this off returns page content as it is.
configuration.security.confirmCookies.de: Ask before an agent sets cookies with `browser_set_cookies`, naming every cookie. Cookies are still limited to the site the tab is on. Turning this off lets an agent set them without a question — which a page could use to sign you into someone else's account.
configuration.chat.defaultAgent.descript: The agent a new chat starts with until you pick one in the chat's agent menu; after that, your last choice is used. The agent has to be installed and signed in, or the chat starts with the first agent that is.
